title: Anonymization of multi-word sequences
author: Participant 1

comments.author: Participant 2
comments.body:
Done in 71d20af and ea39db2.

Now if you select multiple tokens and add a tag, the tokens will be grouped.

![screen shot 2018-10-12 at 07 34 54](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1454404/46850143-f9b57a80-cdf2-11e8-8ca7-5adca02ad57c.png) ... becomes ... ![screen shot 2018-10-12 at 07 35 12](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1454404/46850145-fae6a780-cdf2-11e8-95a5-8a7734c736fe.png)

Note that tokens are grouped even if they are not consecutive, so if I select "Alice" and "Alice's" and then set a tag, then this will happen:

![screen shot 2018-10-12 at 07 47 54](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1454404/46850185-29fd1900-cdf3-11e8-8c06-48daec6aec3e.png)

This is probably not useful, but it is the easiest way to do this. If it is a requirement, we can also check for consecutive-ness.

comments.author: Participant 3
comments.body:
The first example is perfect! 
The second one is slightly problematic since we want to add a "genitive case" tag to the "firstname:female" tag for Alice's. 

But I think this should be tested first before changing

comments.author: Participant 2
comments.body: Fixed this, so the second case (in my last comment) will not happen. Edges will only be grouped if their tokens are consecutive.
